prompt.context_jp: 長い入院を経て、彼女の執行役員就任___内定したそうだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 長い入院を経て、彼女の執行役員就任___内定したそうだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this newly-reported information.

feedback.correct_en: The clause introduces a fresh piece of news — her appointment has been informally confirmed. New information presented in a subordinate clause typically takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the appointment as an already-known topic, which clashes with そうだ reporting new info. を doesn't fit with the intransitive 内定した.

contrast_examples.en: As for the appointment, it's confirmed. (presupposes topic)

prompt.context_jp: ロビーの照明___柔らかく、それでいて主賓ひとりを浮かび上がらせるように調整されている。
prompt.prompt_jp: ロビーの照明___柔らかく…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the sentence topic.

feedback.correct_en: The lobby lighting is the established topic the sentence comments on — it's soft and adjusted a certain way. は marks this topic framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the lighting as new/identified info, but here the narrator is describing a known scene element. に marks location/direction, not applicable.

contrast_examples.en: The lighting (as for it) is soft.
It's the lighting that is soft. (identifies which)

prompt.context_jp: 時計の針だけ___場を支配し、時の流れが妙に滞るように感じられた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時計の針だけ___場を支配し…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits with だけ identifying the sole agent.

feedback.correct_en: Only the clock hands — and nothing else — dominate the space. This exhaustive/exclusive identification pairs with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would be a contrastive topic but weakens the 'only X' exhaustive reading already carried by だけ. に would mark a target/location, not the agent.

contrast_examples.en: As for the clock hands, they move. (topic, non-exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 空調の低い唸りだけ___、無人の椅子の間を縫って響いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 空調の低い唸りだけ___、無人の椅子の間を縫って響いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits with だけ marking the only sound.

feedback.correct_en: Only the hum echoes — nothing else. が emphasizes this exclusive identification of what is doing the action in the silent room.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would be more topical/contrastive and would weaken the vivid exclusivity. で marks means/location, not the subject.

contrast_examples.en: At least the wind was blowing. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 千代の落ち着き払った提案___、二葉の焦燥を和らげるどころか一層かき立てた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 千代の落ち着き払った提案___、二葉の焦燥を和らげるどころか一層かき立てた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames the proposal as the discussed topic.

feedback.correct_en: The proposal was just introduced in the previous line, so it's now the topic being commented on across the clause. は works as a topic marker here, especially with the どころか contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce it as new focus; the narrator is instead elaborating a known element. を would mark a direct object, not the subject.

contrast_examples.en: It was the proposal that backfired. (identificational)

prompt.context_jp: その瞬間、二葉の表情___緩んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: その瞬間、二葉の表情___緩んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking this observed change.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence reports a sudden observable event — her face softened at that instant. Event/change-of-state sentences typically take が on the changing entity.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 表情 a background topic, flattening the sudden-event feel. に doesn't fit the subject slot.

contrast_examples.en: As for her expression, it softened. (sounds like comparison)

prompt.context_jp: 会場に用意された何十脚もの椅子___空席のまま、その空白が糾弾の声をいっそう際立たせる。
prompt.prompt_jp: …何十脚もの椅子___空席のまま…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets the chairs as topic of this commentary.

feedback.correct_en: The chairs are the topic the narrator comments on (they remain empty), contrasted implicitly with what one might expect. は fits the topic + contrastive overtone.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would spotlight the chairs as new info, but they've already been established as part of the venue setup. も would mean 'also/even,' which isn't the intended nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 椅子は空席のままだった。
椅子が空席のままだった。
contrast_examples.en: It was the chairs that remained empty.

prompt.context_jp: 頭取の声___いつになく重かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頭取の声___いつになく重かった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing the president's voice as topic.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator comments on the president's voice (just introduced in the phone call) — a stative description of a known entity. は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce the voice as new focus, but the president is already on the line. を can't mark the subject of a stative adjective.

contrast_examples.en: His voice was heavy. (description of topic)
It was the voice that was heavy. (identificational)

prompt.context_jp: 「去るの___あなたです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「去るの___あなたです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this cleft-like identification.

feedback.correct_en: 'The one who's leaving is YOU' — a cleft structure 〜のは〜だ identifying who. は marks the nominalized topic before the identifying predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would break the cleft structure. を can't mark the subject of です.

prompt.context_jp: 「はぁ？ どうして私___？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「どうして私___？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle expressing 'Why ME (of all people)?'

feedback.correct_en: Futaba demands to know why SHE, specifically, must go — exhaustive identification of the affected person. が carries that 'of all people' focus.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は would sound like 'As for me…' — more detached, missing the indignant exclusive focus. に doesn't mark the subject here.

prompt.context_jp: 「東都銀行のために 長年 尽くしてきた私___ どうして こんな目に 遭わなきゃいけないの！？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…長年 尽くしてきた私___ どうして こんな目に 遭わなきゃいけないの！？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle matching her self-pitying emphasis.

feedback.correct_en: 'Why do I — the one who dedicated years — have to…?' が marks her as the exclusive subject spotlighted against everyone else.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would wrongly make her the direct object. に would mark a destination/recipient, which doesn't fit 遭う's subject slot here.

contrast_examples.jp: 頑張ってきた私がなぜ？
contrast_examples.en: Why me, who worked so hard?
Why do I face this? (more topical, less indignant)

prompt.context_jp: 「室長が裏アカウントを使って ネットに書き込んでいること___ 銀行中にバレたんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…書き込んでいること___ 銀行中にバレたんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle fitting this revelation.

feedback.correct_en: The nominalized fact is new information being revealed — it 'became known.' バレる-type predicates typically take が on the newly-exposed fact.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame it as already-known topic, contradicting バレる (just got exposed). を doesn't fit the subject of バレた (intransitive).

contrast_examples.en: As for the lie, it got exposed. (presupposes)

prompt.context_jp: 誰ひとり二葉を擁護しようとする者___なく、フロアの空気は徐々に凍りついていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰ひとり二葉を擁護しようとする者___なく…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'no one existed who…'

feedback.correct_en: 誰ひとり〜ない patterns strongly prefer は, emphasizing the complete absence as a topic-level contrast ('as for people who'd defend her — none existed').
feedback.incorrect_en: が is grammatical but less idiomatic with 誰ひとり〜ない, which strongly collocates with は for emphatic negation.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰ひとり答える者はいなかった。

prompt.context_jp: 「僕のハンコ___押してある 君が役所に出してくれ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「僕のハンコ___押してある 君が役所に出してくれ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that contrasts his seal with hers.

feedback.correct_en: 'MY seal (at least) is already stamped — YOU take it in.' The implicit contrast between 僕の and 君が makes は the natural contrastive topic marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just identify whose seal without the implied 'as for mine, it's done, now your part.' を would mark the object of 押す but conflicts with the passive-stative 押してある.

prompt.context_jp: 手にした端末には、頭取の名___確かに灯っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: …端末には、頭取の名___確かに灯っている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this observed detail.

feedback.correct_en: The name appearing on the screen is new, observable information — the narrator highlights WHAT is lit up there. が introduces this new discovery.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 頭取の名 a known topic, but the whole point is that we're seeing what's on the display for the first time. に marks location, already used (端末には).

contrast_examples.en: The lamp is lit (as for it).

prompt.context_jp: ひとり分のグラスに注がれたシャンパン___、細かい泡を立てて音もなく弾けている。
prompt.prompt_jp: …シャンパン___、細かい泡を立てて音もなく弾けている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle depicting this vivid scene.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator zooms in on the champagne as a vividly observed, newly presented scene — classic descriptive が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the champagne an abstract topic, losing the cinematic 'look at this' feel. で marks means/location.

contrast_examples.en: Snow is falling (as for it). (odd for scene)

prompt.context_jp: 「あなた___ もう終わりです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あなた___ もう終わりです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle addressing Futaba as topic.

feedback.correct_en: 'As for you — you're finished.' A direct topic-comment statement to the addressee. は is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたが would identify her as 'the one who's finished' among options — too clinical/exhaustive for this confrontational pronouncement. に doesn't fit the predicate.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたはもう終わりだ。
あなたがもう終わりだ。

prompt.context_jp: 都心のホテルの一室に、鈴木二葉の名を___祝賀会の看板が静かに掲げられていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鈴木二葉の名を___祝賀会の看板
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'a sign bearing her name'?

feedback.correct_en: 名を冠する is a set expression meaning 'to bear/be named after.' It's the idiomatic literary choice for a formal event named after someone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 被る/かぶせる literally mean 'to wear/put on top' and don't carry the 'named after' idiomatic meaning here.

contrast_examples.jp: 創業者の名を冠した賞
contrast_examples.en: an award bearing the founder's name

prompt.context_jp: 二葉は___を隠せず、部屋の中央を何度も行き来した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 二葉は___を隠せず…
prompt.prompt_en: What emotion fits a woman pacing when no guests arrive?

feedback.correct_en: 苛立ちを隠せず ('couldn't hide her irritation') is a natural collocation for someone pacing restlessly as guests fail to arrive.
feedback.incorrect_en: 喜び (joy) contradicts her pacing frustration. 眠気 (sleepiness) isn't something one typically 'hides' in this register.

prompt.context_jp: 「夜は長うございますから 先に___はいかがですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「先に___はいかがですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which honorific verb form fits Chiyo's polished suggestion?

feedback.correct_en: なさる is the respectful (尊敬語) form of する, fitting a secretary addressing her superior. 乾杯なさってはいかがですか elevates the addressee's action.
feedback.incorrect_en: 乾杯して is plain and inappropriately casual for Chiyo's register. 乾杯させて would mean 'let me toast' — wrong direction (humble/causative).

contrast_examples.jp: お座りになってください

prompt.context_jp: 「お___のとおりでございます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「お___のとおりでございます」
prompt.prompt_en: Which polite set phrase means 'as you surmise'?

feedback.correct_en: お察しのとおり is a set polite phrase meaning 'just as you surmise/guess,' commonly used in formal service and business Japanese.
feedback.incorrect_en: お見えのとおり isn't idiomatic. お考えのとおり exists but means 'as you think/plan' — doesn't fit the 'guessing a surprise' moment.

prompt.context_jp: ___も積もれば山となるという言葉のとおり、二葉が長年ばら撒いてきた小さな悪意は…
prompt.prompt_jp: ___も積もれば山となる
prompt.prompt_en: Complete this proverb.

feedback.correct_en: 塵も積もれば山となる ('even dust piled up becomes a mountain') is a classic proverb — small things accumulate into something significant.
feedback.incorrect_en: 雪 and 水 can pile up physically but aren't the words in this fixed proverb.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.
A journey of 1000 miles begins with one step.

prompt.context_jp: 「執行役員の話は ___に戻す 以上！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「執行役員の話は ___に戻す」
prompt.prompt_en: Which idiom means 'back to square one / nullified'?

feedback.correct_en: 白紙に戻す ('return to blank paper') is a fixed business/formal idiom meaning to scrap/nullify an agreement.
feedback.incorrect_en: 元気に戻す would mean 'restore to health' — wrong register and meaning. 黒字 means 'in the black (profit),' unrelated.

prompt.context_jp: 「秘書のリーダーが 人の秘密を暴いて ネットにさらすなんて ___！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「…ネットにさらすなんて ___！」
prompt.prompt_en: Which four-character phrase means 'absolutely outrageous'?

feedback.correct_en: 言語道断 means 'outrageous / beyond words,' the right strong condemnation here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一石二鳥 ('two birds with one stone') is positive. 七転八倒 means 'writhing in agony,' unrelated.

prompt.context_jp: 「___ですよ」(二葉の自滅について)
prompt.prompt_en: Which 4-character phrase fits 'she brought it on herself'?

feedback.correct_en: 自業自得 means 'reaping what one sowed' — exactly the secretaries' verdict on Futaba's downfall.
feedback.incorrect_en: 自画自賛 means 'self-praise.' 自由自在 means 'with complete freedom.' Neither fits a karmic-downfall comment.

prompt.context_jp: Miwa, the hotel secretary, greets Director Suzuki at her celebration.
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting sounds more natural for a hotel staff member to a VIP guest of honor?

choices.text: 鈴木室長さま この度は おめでとうございます
鈴木さん おめでとう 今日はよろしく

feedback.correct_en: At a formal celebration in a hotel, staff address a VIP with title + さま and use この度は おめでとうございます — the established formal congratulations formula.
feedback.incorrect_en: Dropping the title and using plain おめでとう with よろしく sounds casual-colleague, inappropriate for hotel-staff-to-VIP register.

contrast_examples.jp: この度はおめでとうございます

prompt.context_jp: Nana informs Futaba that the bank president is on the phone.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits a secretary announcing an incoming call to her boss?

choices.text: 頭取と お電話が つながっております
頭取から 電話 来てるよ

feedback.correct_en: 〜ております is the humble/polite form a secretary uses when reporting to a superior. お電話がつながっております is the standard business formulation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 電話 来てるよ is casual peer-to-peer speech; inappropriate from a secretary to her director.

contrast_examples.jp: お電話がつながっております

prompt.context_jp: Chiyo closes out the hotel bill at the end of the disastrous party.
prompt.prompt_en: Which closing line sounds natural from a high-end hotel secretary to a departing (ex-)client?

choices.text: 本日は 当ホテルを ご利用くださいまして 誠に ありがとうございました
今日は うちのホテル 使ってくれて 本当にありがとう

feedback.correct_en: ご利用くださいまして + 誠にありがとうございました is standard hospitality 敬語 — appropriate for a hotel settling a bill.
feedback.incorrect_en: 使ってくれて 本当にありがとう is casual spoken Japanese — wrong register for a hotel's formal farewell.

contrast_examples.jp: ご利用くださいましてありがとうございました
来てくれてありがとう

prompt.context_jp: Nana coldly cuts ties with Futaba, mimicking Futaba's own ruthless style while keeping outward politeness.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line better captures Nana's ironic 'polite betrayal' tone?

choices.text: あなたに教わったとおり 要らなくなった人間は切り捨てます お世話になりました
あなたの教え通り いらない人間を切り捨てる 今までどうも

feedback.correct_en: The chapter line keeps 敬語 (切り捨てます / お世話になりました) — this politeness-as-weapon is the hallmark of Nana's turn. The 敬語 veneer makes the betrayal chilling.
feedback.incorrect_en: The plain-form variant drops into casual speech and loses the exquisite irony of maintaining polite service register while stabbing her boss.

prompt.context_jp: The secretaries' motto about keeping confidences.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is the natural idiom for 'take secrets to the grave'?

choices.text: 秘密は墓場まで 持っていきます
秘密は死ぬまで 隠しておきます

feedback.correct_en: 墓場まで持っていく is the established Japanese idiom equivalent to 'take to the grave.' It's the standard phrasing in such oaths.
feedback.incorrect_en: 死ぬまで隠す is grammatical but lacks the idiomatic punch and recognizability of the 墓場まで phrase.

contrast_examples.jp: 秘密を墓場まで持っていく
contrast_examples.en: take a secret to the grave
